- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–15% relative to recent history.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 3–8% if recent 7–14 day average is trending higher.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day spikes; smooth out forecast volatility by applying a 3–5 day moving average filter to model output.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in the last 7 days, apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% per day to prevent mean reversion miss.
- For forecasts with high variance (std > 3% of mean), apply a volatility cap: cap forecast at ±1.5× standard deviation from recent 14-day mean to avoid extreme outliers.
- When true outcome is below forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid underestimating rebound potential.
